paragraphs.text: Serve the DeepSeek Harness (dsh) Web UI through a non-localhost authority: trusted hosts, loopback p
age parity, pinned launch token, no patching.
# dsh-dev-plugins
A growing collection of plugins for the DeepSeek Harness (dsh), installed as one bundle. The current
release serves the dsh Web UI through a **non-localhost authority** — a reverse proxy, SSH tunnel,
or LAN address — without patching the installed dsh, and adds browser notifications, a workspace tok
en-usage page, and a composer where Enter inserts a line break.
中文文档
## What this fixes
Stock `dsh web` is built for a browser on the same machine. Six things are missing or break when the
browser reaches it through another authority:
| Problem | Stock dsh | This plugin |
| `/api` Host/Origin fence | accepts loopback, the listener's bind literal, and `--trusted-host` onl
y; every RPC answers `403` for a proxy authority | appends `DSH_DEV_PLUGINS_TRUSTED_HOSTS` authoriti

es to the same list (`--trusted-host` keeps working) |
| Page view (`connection.isLoopback`) | deriv
ed from `location.hostname`; a proxied page is treated as non-loopback, so on dsh 0.2.0 settings sta
y in process-local memory (`settings are unavailable in this browser` on the Models page) and on eve
ry version the host-document action is hidden | injects `__DSH_TRANSPORT__ = { ownsHost: true }`, th
e host-owned transport hook dsh already uses for its desktop shell, so authenticated pages report th

e loopback view |
| Launch token | random per process; the only way to find the login URL after a re

start is the service log | pins `DSH_WEB_TOKEN` (or plugin config) across restarts |
| First login |
opening the bare deployment URL answers a plain `401`, so the token must come from the printed `?to
ken=` URL | serves an HTML token form on the bare URL (`loginPage`, default on) and feeds the submit

ted token back into the stock exchange |
| Background attention | a finished session or a pending ap
proval/question stays invisible while the tab is in the background | raises a Web Notification for c

ompletion and for pending input (`notifications`, default on) |
| Token usage history | the chat sta
ts strip only shows the open Session; there is no workspace or cross-session view | adds a sidebar *
*Token usage** page that aggregates provider-billed tokens by workspace and day from the Host's dura
ble session logs (`statsPage`, default on) |
[该节后续省略]
## How it works
[该节后续省略]
## Security
- **The launch token is the credential.** Anyone holding the printed `?token=` URL can obtain a sess
ion cookie and full owner access. Share it deliberately. A pinned token is a long-lived credential —
never commit it. Changing `DSH_WEB_TOKEN` and restarting invalidates the old URL but does **not** r
evoke cookies already issued (they live for `cookieMaxAgeDays`, 30 days by default); clear the site'

s cookies, or remove the browser-session credential record and restart, to revoke them.
- **Trusted
hosts are not authentication.** They only admit the authority to the Host/Origin fence; the signed s
ession cookie still gates every RPC. Never expose the listener port to an untrusted network without

TLS and a proxy you control.
- **Loopback parity is a privilege decision.** On dsh 0.2.0 it makes se
ttings host-backed for authenticated remote browsers; on every version it exposes local-only UI affo
rdances such as **Open configuration file**, which opens the settings document in the *host's* edito
r. Remote browsers already hold owner credentials, but operators who want the stock least-privilege

view can set `loopback: false`.
- **The loopback view goes beyond a documented client contract.** Up
stream documents `ownsHost` as reserved for a shell that assembles its own transport and says served
pages never carry the global. This bundle sets it anyway; every current dsh consumer reads it only
for `isLoopback`, but a future or third-party client plugin could treat it as proof of host ownershi

p. `loopback: false` removes that exposure.
- **Plain HTTP leaks the token.** Terminate TLS at the p

roxy or with `--tls-cert/--tls-key`; the upstream guide covers cookie `Secure` behaviour.
- **The lo
gin form does not rate-limit.** It only reveals an input for the same high-entropy launch token the
printed URL carries; a proxy-level rate limit is still the right control for exposed endpoints. The

form never renders for an authority the Host/Origin fence rejects.
[该节后续省略]
## Compatibility
- Tested against dsh `0.2.2-rc.1` (both halves on all three deployed endpoints; the login and settin
gs flows were exercised on the workstation origin and its `:9443` proxy), `0.2.1-rc.2`, `0.2.1-rc.3`

, and `0.2.0-rc.2` (Web profile).
- Declared range: `engines.dsh >=0.2.0-0 <0.3.0-0`. dsh 0.1.x is n
ot supported or tested, and dsh 0.3.x stays outside the range until the plugin is verified against i
t. dsh 0.2.2 evaluates the range with prereleases participating, so `0.2.2-rc.1` passes the compatib

ility gate without a version exemption (install and boot share that evaluator).
- On dsh 0.2.0 a pro
file-level wildcard bind (`webserver.host: 0.0.0.0`) derives LAN authorities; the patch preserves th

em, so the printed LAN URL works without extra trusted-host entries.
- The plugin row is Web-profile
only; in a profile without a `connection` service the row stays inactive, so installing it there ac

hieves nothing.
- `npm install -g @deepseek-ai/dsh@<version>` replaces the dsh install but not the p

rofile: the plugin keeps working after a dsh upgrade. Restart `dsh web` to load a new dsh version.
-
The token seam reads `connection.browserAuth.launchToken`. If dsh changes that shape, the plugin th

rows at boot when a token is configured; unset the token or update the plugin.
- Browser control nee
ds Chrome 120+ with the extension loaded unpacked. The `debugger` permission shows Chrome's automati
on banner while a tab is attached. On a headless server there is no Chrome, so the bridge stays idle

and the tools fail with `bridge_disconnected`.
- The patch resolves `bridge/index.js` from `$DSH_HO
ME` and `$DSH_PROFILE`; a host that launches `dsh web` without those environment variables falls bac
k to `~/.dsh` and the `web` profile. A different profile name therefore needs the variable set (the

stock CLI exports both).
- The composer Enter rewrite depends on dsh-internal DOM markers (`[data-co
mposer-card]`, `[data-lexical-editor="true"]`, `[data-trigger-menu]`). If a future dsh release renam
es them, the listener finds no composer and silently no-ops, restoring stock Enter-sends; it never b

reaks the page.
[该节后续省略]
